verses.text: When Jesus had finished saying all these things, he said to his followers,
"As you know, the Passover festival is two days away. The Son of Man will be handed over to be nailed to a cross."
Then the chief priests, the teachers of the law and the elders of the people met in the palace of the high priest, whose name was Caiaphas.
They made a plan to arrest Jesus in a secret way and kill him.
"But not during the festival," they said, "or the people may start a riot."
Jesus was in Bethany, in the home of a man known as Simon the leper.
A woman came to him with a beautiful jar of very expensive perfume. She poured it on his head while he was sitting at the table.
When the followers saw this, they were angry. "Why this waste?" they asked.
"This perfume could have been sold for a lot of money, and the money given to poor people."
Jesus knew what they were saying, and he said to them, "Why are you bothering this woman? She has done a beautiful thing for me.
You will always have poor people with you, but you will not always have me.
When she poured this perfume on my body, she did it to prepare me for my burial.
I tell you for certain, wherever this good news is preached in the whole world, what she has done will also be told, so that people will remember her."
Then one of the twelve followers, the one called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests.
He asked, "What will you give me if I hand him over to you?" So they counted out for him thirty silver coins.
From then on, Judas watched for a chance to hand Jesus over to them.
On the first day of the Festival of Bread Made Without Yeast, the followers came to Jesus. They asked, "Where do you want us to prepare for you to eat the Passover meal?"
He replied, "Go into the city to a certain man and tell him, 'The Teacher says: My time is near. I am going to celebrate the Passover with my followers at your house.'"
So the followers did what Jesus had told them, and they prepared the Passover meal.
When evening came, Jesus was at the table with the twelve followers.
While they were eating, he said, "I tell you for certain, one of you will hand me over to my enemies."
They were very sad. One after the other they began to say to him, "Surely you do not mean me, Lord?"
Jesus replied, "The one who has dipped his hand into the bowl with me will hand me over.
The Son of Man will go, just as it is written about him. But how terrible it will be for the man who hands over the Son of Man! It would be better for him if he had never been born."
Then Judas, the one who would hand him over, said, "Surely you do not mean me, Rabbi?" Jesus answered, "You have said so."
While they were eating, Jesus took bread and gave thanks. He broke it and gave it to his followers. He said, "Take this and eat it. This is my body."
Then he took the cup and gave thanks, and he gave it to them. He said, "All of you drink from it.
This is my blood of the new covenant. It is poured out for many people so that their sins can be forgiven.
I tell you, I will not drink wine again from now on until the day I drink it new with you in my Father's kingdom."
When they had sung a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
Then Jesus told them, "This very night you will all run away and leave me. It is written: 'I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered.'
But after I have been raised to life, I will go ahead of you into Galilee."
Peter replied, "Even if all the others run away because of you, I never will."
"I tell you for certain," Jesus answered, "this very night, before the rooster crows, you will say three times that you do not know me."
But Peter said, "Even if I have to die with you, I will never say I do not know you." And all the other followers said the same.
Then Jesus went with his followers to a place called Gethsemane. He said to them, "Sit here while I go over there and pray."
He took Peter and the two sons of Zebedee with him. He began to feel very sad and troubled.
Then he said to them, "My soul is so full of sadness that I feel close to death. Stay here and keep watch with me."
He went a little further and fell with his face to the ground. He prayed, "My Father, if it is possible, take this cup of suffering away from me. But let what you want be done, not what I want."
Then he went back to his followers and found them sleeping. "Could you not keep watch with me for one hour?" he asked Peter.
"Keep watch and pray, so that you will not give in to temptation. The spirit is willing, but the body is weak."
He went away a second time and prayed, "My Father, if this cup cannot be taken away unless I drink it, may what you want be done."
When he came back, he again found them sleeping, because their eyes were heavy.
So he left them and went away once more. He prayed the third time, saying the same thing.
Then he came back to the followers and said to them, "Are you still sleeping and resting? Look, the time has come. The Son of Man is being handed over to sinners.
Get up! Let's go! Here comes the man who is handing me over!"
While Jesus was still speaking, Judas, one of the twelve, arrived. With him was a large crowd carrying swords and clubs. They had been sent by the chief priests and the elders of the people.
The man who was handing Jesus over had arranged a signal with them. "The one I kiss is the man," he had said. "Arrest him."
Going straight to Jesus, Judas said, "Greetings, Rabbi!" and kissed him.
Jesus replied, "Friend, do what you came for." Then the men stepped forward, grabbed Jesus and arrested him.
At that moment one of Jesus' companions reached for his sword and pulled it out. He struck the servant of the high priest and cut off his ear.
"Put your sword back in its place," Jesus said to him. "All who use the sword will die by the sword.
Do you think I cannot ask my Father for help? He would send me more than twelve armies of angels straight away.
But then how would the Scriptures come true that say it must happen this way?"
At that time Jesus said to the crowd, "Am I leading a rebellion, that you have come out with swords and clubs to capture me? Every day I sat in the temple courts teaching, and you did not arrest me.
But all this has happened so that the words of the prophets in the Scriptures would come true." Then all the followers left him and ran away.
The men who had arrested Jesus took him to Caiaphas the high priest. The teachers of the law and the elders had gathered there.
But Peter followed him at a distance, right up to the courtyard of the high priest. He went in and sat down with the guards to see what would happen.
The chief priests and the whole council were looking for false evidence against Jesus, so that they could put him to death.
But they did not find any, even though many false witnesses came forward. Finally two men came forward.
They said, "This man said, 'I can destroy the temple of God and build it again in three days.'"
Then the high priest stood up and said to Jesus, "Are you not going to answer? What is this these men are saying against you?"
But Jesus stayed silent. The high priest said to him, "I order you to swear by the living God and tell us if you are the Christ, the Son of God."
"You have said so," Jesus replied. "But I tell all of you, from now on you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right side of the Mighty One and coming on the clouds of heaven."
Then the high priest tore his clothes and said, "He has insulted God! Why do we need any more witnesses? Look, now you have heard him insult God.
What do you think?" "He deserves to die!" they answered.
Then they spat in his face and hit him with their fists. Others slapped him
and said, "Prophesy to us, Christ! Who hit you?"
Peter was sitting out in the courtyard. A servant girl came to him. "You also were with Jesus of Galilee," she said.
But he denied it in front of all of them. "I do not know what you are talking about," he said.
Then he went out to the gateway, where another servant girl saw him. She said to the people there, "This man was with Jesus of Nazareth."
He denied it again and swore, "I do not know the man!"
After a little while, those standing there went up to Peter. "You must be one of them," they said. "The way you talk gives you away."
Then he began to call down curses on himself, and he swore to them, "I do not know the man!" Straight away a rooster crowed.
Then Peter remembered what Jesus had said: "Before the rooster crows, you will say three times that you do not know me." And he went outside and cried bitterly.
